subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — DPA scope, SCCs, and export addendum
messages:
From: Hannah Ross <hannah.ross@medbridge.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, MedBridge Procurement <procurement@medbridge.com>
Cc: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@medbridge.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:43:00Z
Subject: Initial redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our consolidated redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (see MSA_DPA_redlines_v3.docx and OrderForm_MedBridge-track_changes.pdf). A couple specific asks from legal that I want to highlight so we can avoid surprises in procurement: 

- MedBridge needs to confirm the data transfer mechanism: they prefer SCCs + UK Addendum where applicable, and want explicit callout of the export addendum if data leaves the EEA/UK.
- They would like the DPA to list MedBridge as Controller and Redwood as Processor for the hosted API use case; however they have a separate use case for a private/on-prem deployment where roles may be reversed for certain data flows — we need to confirm mapping.
- There is a request for the subprocessor approval clause to include a 5-business-day notification window before new subprocessor onboarding and a right to object escalation path.

Can you confirm next steps and an expected timeline for legal review? Procurement is trying to close SOW pricing by 12/15.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Ross
Head of Legal Operations
MedBridge Health

Date: 2026-12-02T11:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for sending these over and flagging the high-priority items. We can support SCCs + UK Addendum where required; I want to loop in legal to confirm the controller/processor language and the subprocessor notification window you requested.

Planned next steps on our side: 
- Internal legal review of redlines (Ben/Laura) and prepare a proposed clean DPA that reconciles the controller/processor table and the export addendum language.
- Confirm whether the private/on-prem flow requires a separate Annex A to the DPA (we suspect it will).
- Provide a draft response and a short summary of outstanding asks for your team by 12/04.

I have attached the redlines you sent to our internal folder and added an SCCs_matrix.xlsx where we map the modules we expect to propose (Module 2 for Processor-to-Controller flows; Module 1 where Redwood acts as Controller in narrow circumstances).

Ben/Laura/Karthik — please prioritize this. Procurement timeline looks like 12/15 close. If we need to escalate an exception for the 5-business-day notification (client requested), flag here and I will route to Head of Revenue.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: analysis of MedBridge redlines (DPA / SCCs / export addendum)

Priya / Laura / Karthik —

I reviewed Hannah's redlines and the two items that need negotiation with the customer are (1) the controller/processor mapping for the two deployment modes, and (2) the 5-business-day subprocessor notice + objection right. Quick summary below with recommended language and risk posture: 

1) Controller/Processor mapping
- For hosted API: keep Master DPA that lists MedBridge as Controller and Redwood as Processor. Add Annex A with a table showing data categories and flow mapping. This is low risk but needs to be explicit so procurement can reconcile with their privacy team.
- For Private/on-prem: propose a carveout Annex B (transfer addendum) that states when customer operates private deployment and directly controls hosting, the roles for customer-managed data streams will be Controller/Processor inverted for those streams. Add a sentence retaining Redwood's obligation for any processing performed on Redwood-managed control plane telemetry (e.g., logs).

2) SCCs / export mechanism
- Recommend offering SCCs Module 2 for the main flows and providing the UK Addendum as requested. Add a paragraph in the export addendum that lists fallback for non-EU jurisdictions and confirms appropriate technical and organisational safeguards.

3) Subprocessor notice / objection
- 5-business-day absolute right is operationally risky for platform-managed subprocessors. Recommend: 10-business-day notification and a defined reasonable-objection process that defaults to mediation/escalation to legal rather than an immediate bar. If MedBridge insists on 5 days, we should request a narrow carveout for security-critical subprocessors where notification is 5 days but automatic objection is limited to documented material concerns.

Action items I will produce by EOD 12/04: clean marked DPA that reconciles the table, a redlined export addendum paragraph, and a short rationale memo for commercial on the subprocessor timing so sales/procurement can set expectations.

Ben Carter
Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: proposed_DPA_clean_v1.docx (will upload), export_addendum_paragraph.txt
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, MedBridge Procurement <procurement@medbridge.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — next steps and proposed concessions

Hannah / Oliver —

Following internal review, please find the vendor-side proposals and our requested confirmation items: 

1) Controller/Processor annexes — attached: a draft Annex A (hosted) and Annex B (private deployment transfer addendum). These clarify which data categories map to which roles. Please confirm whether the private deployment carveout covers your 'on-prem telemetry' use case or whether you want separate language for clinical data vs. operational logs.

2) SCCs & UK Addendum — Redwood will accept SCCs Module 2 for cross-border flows and will include the UK Addendum where applicable. The attached SCCs_matrix.xlsx shows our default modules per flow. If MedBridge requires Module 1 for any flow, flag which flows/fields.

3) Subprocessor notice window — proposed compromise: 10-business-day notice with an objection escalation path to legal. For security-critical subprocessors (e.g., key management providers), we can agree to 5-business-day notice but objections should be limited to documented material risks. If MedBridge cannot accept this, please state specific subprocessors or business rationale and we will escalate.

4) Timeline & signing — procurement asked for a 12/15 close. If the controller/processor confirmation and subprocessor timing are agreed by 12/10, Ben will finalize the redlines and we can issue a DocuSign packet. DocuSign preview: https://docusign.net/preview/DEAL-2026-MB-1234

Please reply with the single-line confirmations requested above (controller mapping ok / SCCs modules ok / subprocessor notice ok) so we can move to final redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0199
